text:
eli: Quick experiment note — I pushed a prototype 'windowed rejector' to canary today. Idea: track a short sliding window of admit rate, and smooth rejections over 500ms buckets instead of doing abrupt sheds. Config attached.

eli: Config snippet:```yaml
admit_controller:
  mode: windowed_rejector
  window_ms: 500
  smoothing_alpha: 0.25
  token_budget_target: 1200  # tokens/sec per lane
  backlog_thresholds:
    low: 40
    high: 200
  drop_probation_ms: 2000
```

eli: Deploy notes: canary on pool-gamma, kernel=v2.1-optimized, batching=continuous with batch_max=64

jasmin: Nice. What's the rationale for smoothing_alpha=0.25?

eli: Picked to be responsive but avoid oscillation. We saw alpha=0.5 flip-flop under synthetic spikes. 0.25 keeps reject ramp gentle.

tom: Observations after 30m: tail P99 latency down ~8% under steady 200rps workload, but we see a higher variance when KV cache miss rate climbs >12%.

eli: Did you get profiler traces? flamegraph link?

tom: Uploaded here: https://internal/fgs/windowed-rejector-30m.svg — look at CPU slices during mid-spike. Notably, kernel-selection stalls appear correlated with admission churn.

kevin: I pulled sampling logs. When KV miss >12% we start seeing more batch fragmentation: avg batch size drops from 24->11, and that increases per-request kernel warmups.

jasmin: So smoothing helps latency only if batches stay large. With KV miss-induced fragmentation the controller still rejects but doesn't help much.

eli: Agree. One idea: couple the windowed rejector with a transient 'batch_coalesce_hold' flag when miss-rate spikes — hold incoming requests for an extra 20ms to rebuild batch density. Thoughts?

sachin: I'm wary of explicit holds — that can violate low-latency SLOs for small queries. But if we gate it by predicted kernel-switch cost it might be ok. Add a heuristic: if expected kernel swap cost > 2ms and estimated coalesced batch size increase > 30% then hold up to max_hold_ms=30.

tom: Quick numbers: in canary, enabling hold=20ms at miss>15% restored batch size to 20 and cut P99 by ~15% but P50 went up by ~6ms for affected requests.

kevin: Also measured downstream 429 churn — smoothing reduced immediate 429 storms but extended the window where clients saw elevated retry latencies. Need to tune client-side backoff guidance.

eli: Good point. We should avoid making clients keep hammering during the smoothed period. Suggest we emit an advisory header X-RW-Backoff: "smoothed" when we intentionally delay/admit at a lower rate. Ops can route retry logic to exponential backoff on that header.

jasmin: Can we correlate kernel hinting? If runtime can tag batches with kernel_hints (e.g., fp16-quant, small-kernel), maybe the controller can favor lanes that maintain kernel affinity. That would reduce swap cost and make coalescing more effective.

sachin: That's feasible. Need an API between admission controller and kernel-selection: controller provides a preferred kernel_hint and kernel selection returns estimated swap_penalty_ms. We can incorporate swap_penalty into token_budget_target.

eli: Action items: 1) sachin to prototype kernel_hint handshake (PR incoming). 2) kevin to add coalesce_hold boolean gated by miss-rate + swap_penalty. 3) jasmin to draft client header and SDK guidance. 4) tom to run 6h soak with traffic mix A/B.

tom: Starting soak now. I'll post perf dashboards in ~3h and final after 6h.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started: admit-controller v0.3.2 -> pool-gamma. CI checks passed. :rocket:

kevin: FYI found a perf regression in v2.1-optimized kernel: when batch size<8 kernel selection path does extra memcpy, adding ~1.8ms. Filed issue #INF-894. Might explain small-batch penalty.

eli: Thanks — that's likely the missing piece. If we fix memcpy leak, coalesce_hold will be more effective.

jasmin: One more thought — token_budget_target currently global per lane. We could make it adaptive per-client-class (interactive vs. batch) so interactive stays lower-latency while batch gets coalesced. That reduces cross-traffic interference.

sachin: Agreed. Let's keep that in the next iteration. For now I'll wire kernel_hint and swap_penalty into the admit calculation.

eli: Great. Keep updates here. If soak looks good we'll roll to canary-2 with memcopy fix and adaptive token budgets. :thumbsup:
